claim: Blocking 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD) in the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway resulted in substantial reduction of Tregs suppressive function.
source: Here, we showed that blocking 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD) in the oxidative PPP resulted in substantial reduction of Tregs suppressive function and shifts toward Th1, Th2, and Th17 phenotypes which led to the development of fetal inflammatory disorder in mice model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, which is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript including mouse models and in vitro assays.

claim: Blocking 6PGD in Tregs caused shifts toward Th1, Th2, and Th17 phenotypes.
source: Here, we showed that blocking 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD) in the oxidative PPP resulted in substantial reduction of Tregs suppressive function and shifts toward Th1, Th2, and Th17 phenotypes which led to the development of fetal inflammatory disorder in mice model.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by gene expression data, flow cytometry, and cytokine measurements shown in Figures 1-3.

claim: Blocking 6PGD in Tregs led to the development of fatal inflammatory disorder in mice model.
source: Here, we showed that blocking 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD) in the oxidative PPP resulted in substantial reduction of Tregs suppressive function and shifts toward Th1, Th2, and Th17 phenotypes which led to the development of fetal inflammatory disorder in mice model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is demonstrated by the phenotype of Pgdfl/flFoxp3Cre mice shown in Figure 1.

claim: Blocking 6PGD in Tregs improved anti-tumor responses.
source: These in turn improved anti-tumor responses and worsened the outcomes of colitis model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by tumor growth data in Figure 3 showing reduced tumor volume and weight in 6PGD-deficient Treg mice.

claim: Blocking 6PGD in Tregs worsened the outcomes of colitis model.
source: These in turn improved anti-tumor responses and worsened the outcomes of colitis model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by IBD model data in Figure 2 showing increased weight loss and colon damage.

claim: 6PGD blocked Tregs showed improved glycolysis.
source: Metabolically, 6PGD blocked Tregs showed improved glycolysis and enhanced non-oxidative PPP to support nucleotide biosynthesis.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by ECAR measurements and SIRM analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: 6PGD blocked Tregs showed enhanced non-oxidative PPP to support nucleotide biosynthesis.
source: Metabolically, 6PGD blocked Tregs showed improved glycolysis and enhanced non-oxidative PPP to support nucleotide biosynthesis.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by stable isotope tracing data showing increased R5P and nucleotide synthesis in Figure 4.

claim: 6PGD plays a critical role in modulating Tregs plasticity and function.
source: These results uncover critical role of 6PGD in modulating Tregs plasticity and function, which qualifies it as a novel metabolic checkpoint for immunotherapy applications.
evidence: The abstract concludes this based on the collective experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: 6PGD qualifies as a novel metabolic checkpoint for immunotherapy applications.
source: These results uncover critical role of 6PGD in modulating Tregs plasticity and function, which qualifies it as a novel metabolic checkpoint for immunotherapy applications.
evidence: The abstract proposes this based on the demonstrated effects of 6PGD blockade on Treg function and anti-tumor responses.

claim: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) limit inflammatory responses by suppressing self-reactive T cells to maintain balance between protective and excessive inflammation.
source: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are distinct subsets of CD4+ T cells that limit inflammatory responses by suppressing self-reactive T cells to maintain balance between protective and excessive inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Treg function.

claim: Lipid oxidation and the mevalonate pathway are considered key to Tregs functions.
source: Although lipid oxidation and the mevalonate pathway being considered key to their functions (Michalek et al., 2011; Timilshina et al., 2019), cellular metabolism in Tregs is an active area of investigation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies (Michalek et al., 2011; Timilshina et al., 2019).

claim: Tregs depend on lipid oxidation and mevalonate pathways to maintain their suppressive functions.
source: Tregs depend on these pathways to maintain their suppressive functions, which are distinct from the high glycolytic signatures of conventional CD4+ effector subsets, Th1, Th2, and Th17 (Michalek et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Michalek et al., 2011.

claim: Conventional CD4+ effector subsets Th1, Th2, and Th17 have high glycolytic signatures.
source: Tregs depend on these pathways to maintain their suppressive functions, which are distinct from the high glycolytic signatures of conventional CD4+ effector subsets, Th1, Th2, and Th17 (Michalek et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Michalek et al., 2011.

claim: Glycolysis is critical for Treg expansion.
source: Although glycolysis is not major feature in Tregs, it is critical for Treg expansion (Pacella et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Pacella et al., 2018.

claim: Glucose enters the cell via glucose transporter 1 (Glut1) and is metabolized to glucose 6-phosphate (G6P).
source: Glucose (Glc) enters the cell via glucose transporter 1 (Glut1) and is metabolized to glucose 6-phosphate (G6P), which has alternative fates via glycolysis and as the entry point into the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: G6P has alternative fates via glycolysis and as the entry point into the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP).
source: Glucose (Glc) enters the cell via glucose transporter 1 (Glut1) and is metabolized to glucose 6-phosphate (G6P), which has alternative fates via glycolysis and as the entry point into the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The PPP comprises two interdependent branches: the oxidative branch and the non-oxidative branch.
source: The PPP, also known as the hexose monophosphate shunt or phosphogluconate pathway, comprises two interdependent branches: the oxidative branch and the non-oxidative branch.
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Oxidative PPP is composed of three essentially irreversible reactions.
source: Oxidative PPP is composed of three essentially irreversible reactions in which the first is catalyzed by G6PD that converts G6P to 6-phosphogluconolactone (6PGL) while generating reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: G6PD catalyzes the first reaction of oxidative PPP that converts G6P to 6-phosphogluconolactone (6PGL) while generating NADPH.
source: Oxidative PPP is composed of three essentially irreversible reactions in which the first is catalyzed by G6PD that converts G6P to 6-phosphogluconolactone (6PGL) while generating reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: 6PGL hydrolyzes to 6-phosphogluconate (6PG).
source: 6PGL then hydrolyzes to 6-phosphogluconate (6PG), which is oxidatively decarboxylated by 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD), producing ribulose-5-phosphate and a second molecule of NADPH and (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: 6PGD oxidatively decarboxylates 6PG, producing ribulose-5-phosphate and a second molecule of NADPH.
source: 6PGL then hydrolyzes to 6-phosphogluconate (6PG), which is oxidatively decarboxylated by 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD), producing ribulose-5-phosphate and a second molecule of NADPH and (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Ribulose-5-phosphate is the precursor for ribose-5-phophate (R5P) and thence nucleotides.
source: Ribulose-5-phosphate is the precursor for ribose-5-phophate (R5P) and thence nucleotides, and NADPH is required both for reductive anabolism and for antioxidative defense.
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: NADPH is required both for reductive anabolism and for antioxidative defense.
source: Ribulose-5-phosphate is the precursor for ribose-5-phophate (R5P) and thence nucleotides, and NADPH is required both for reductive anabolism and for antioxidative defense.
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Tregs are known to have high rates of lipid oxidation.
source: Tregs are known to have high rates of lipid oxidation (Michalek et al., 2011), which would provoke antioxidant machinery which requires NADPH generated from PPP.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Michalek et al., 2011.

claim: High rates of lipid oxidation in Tregs would provoke antioxidant machinery which requires NADPH generated from PPP.
source: Tregs are known to have high rates of lipid oxidation (Michalek et al., 2011), which would provoke antioxidant machinery which requires NADPH generated from PPP.
evidence: This is inferred from the known relationship between lipid oxidation, oxidative stress, and NADPH requirement.

claim: Pharmacological inhibitor of 6PGD (6-aminonicotinamide [6-AN]) enhances IFN-γ production by in vitro activated CD4+ T cells.
source: Our preliminary studies showed that pharmacological inhibitor of 6PGD (6-aminonicotinamide [6-AN]) but not G6PD inhibitor (dehydroepiandrosterone [DHEA]) enhances IFN-γ production by in vitro activated CD4+ T cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: G6PD inhibitor (dehydroepiandrosterone [DHEA]) does not enhance IFN-γ production by in vitro activated CD4+ T cells.
source: Our preliminary studies showed that pharmacological inhibitor of 6PGD (6-aminonicotinamide [6-AN]) but not G6PD inhibitor (dehydroepiandrosterone [DHEA]) enhances IFN-γ production by in vitro activated CD4+ T cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DHEA at 10 µM instigated poor T cells viability.
source: while DHEA but not 6-AN at 10 µM instigated poor T cells viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 6-AN at 10 µM does not instigate poor T cells viability.
source: while DHEA but not 6-AN at 10 µM instigated poor T cells viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Enhanced effector phenotype in Pgdfl/flCd4Cre mice suggests altered regulation of T cell differentiation and/or activation.
source: An enhanced effector phenotype of T CD4+ subsets was observed in Pgdfl/flCd4Cre mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I-J) suggesting altered regulation of T cell differentiation and/or activation.

claim: Pgdfl/flFoxp3Cre mice had a significantly shorter lifespan.
